claims.summary: Over any field, let literal CNF violation products F_i and all Boolean B_j=x_j^2-x_j have Hilbert-like certificate C(x,Y,Z), size S depth d. Put P=product_i(1-F_i), P_i=product_(k!=i)(1-F_k), and literal-telescoping T_i(x,B)=F_i^2-F_i. Then Q=C(x,(-P_i T_i(x,Z))_i,(P Z_j)_j) satisfies Q(x,B)=P, is Hilbert-like and has size O(S+s^3), depth<=d+10, s=m+n+literal length+1, counting gates and wires with unbounded fan-in. Conversely sum_i(product_(k<i)(1-F_k))Y_i+Q gives a certificate with fixed clause coefficients, size O(S+s^3), depth<=max(d,6)+2. Repeated, tautological and empty clauses allowed; polynomial Hilbert-likeness suffices.
claims.assessment: Working explicit formal transformation, medium reviewed. Extends the earlier selector identity by retaining and constructing Boolean corrections from the supplied certificate. Does not supply a certificate from nothing, preserve exact Frege simulation image or give a PC degree bound.
claims.rationale: Isolates the complete Boolean-ideal certificate as an equivalent constant-depth circuit-size target for literal CNFs; it is an equivalent formulation, not goal progress.
claims.next_action: A lower-bound use still needs a size-sensitive obstruction for all full Boolean corrections at the stated depth overhead.

claims.summary: For every identity P=sum_j b_j(x)(x_j^2-x_j) over any field, b_j(a)=(2a_j-1)partial_j P(a) at every Boolean a. All Boolean-point coefficient values are syzygy invariant. For a literal CNF satisfaction product P, r_j=(2x_j-1)partial_jP jointly represent these values with size O(s^3), depth<=8 via the literal product rule. These representatives need not be formal correction coefficients; duplicated inconsistent units give P=B^2, b=B, all traces zero but P formally nonzero.
claims.assessment: Working elementary differentiation identity and all-parameter cheap representatives, checked by same medium reviewer. Values of coefficients, not their higher derivatives, are determined. Compatible with prior finite-jet selector control.
claims.rationale: Rejects using the Boolean-point coefficient vector alone as the hard invariant after normalization; no formal-circuit lower bound.
claims.next_action: Keep full formal corrections and their circuit cost; no further pointwise test is needed.

claims.summary: For any literal CNF satisfaction product H(x_1,...,x_r), append contradictory units on fresh z. Its satisfaction product P=-(z^2-z)H has explicit small constant-depth Boolean certificate Q=-H Z_z. Ordered monic division by B_1,...,B_r,B_z, passing each remainder onward, has final coefficient -ML(H). Thus universal efficient canonical-coefficient extraction even from supplied small certificates would efficiently multilinearize arbitrary CNF satisfaction products.
claims.assessment: Working explicit all-parameter projection, checked by same medium reviewer. A conditional complexity implication, not an unconditional hardness result. A difficult canonical coefficient does not imply certificate hardness, since these padded CNFs have explicit cheap certificates.
claims.rationale: Makes the cost of canonicalization concrete within literal CNFs rather than treating unique normal forms as an efficient circuit extraction.
claims.next_action: Calibrate homogeneous-component extraction on permutation-matrix CNF indicators, keeping field and depth costs.
